summary: Dashboard heatmap card not honoring user timezone and refresh interval leading to stale/shifted buckets
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightAI reports that a time-series heatmap card on their custom dashboard is showing data buckets shifted by the account timezone and does not update when the dashboard auto-refresh interval is changed. The heatmap appears to show older values for the current hour and only refreshes after a manual page reload.

Impact:
- Observability of recent request volumes is incorrect for their engineering on-call.
- Alert evaluations that reference the heatmap-derived metric appear delayed, causing delayed paging for response spikes.
- Affects one customer dashboard and any other dashboards with the same heatmap widget configuration in us-west prod.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (prod/us-west).
- Customer account on Dedicated tier.
- Heatmap widget configured with timezone: account (America/Los_Angeles) and auto-refresh: 30s.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Login to BrightAI account (dedicated prod).
2. Open the custom dashboard with the heatmap card (range: last 3 hours).
3. Observe the heatmap tiles corresponding to the last 60 minutes do not change over 5 minutes.
4. Change auto-refresh from 30s to 15s via the widget settings -> no change.
5. Manually reload the page -> heatmap updates and tiles shift forward to current time.

Expected behavior:
- Heatmap should honor the account timezone when computing bucket boundaries and should auto-refresh at the configured interval without needing a full page reload.

Actual behavior:
- Heatmap buckets appear to be calculated against UTC-aligned boundaries, then shifted client-side using the timezone setting which causes off-by-one-hour display for DST zones. Additionally, the widget's refresh mechanism stops triggering new queries to the analytics pipeline after the dashboard has been open for ~10 minutes, requiring a full reload.

Relevant logs and traces:
- Console frontend logs: heatmap-refresh: failed to schedule refresh after attempt 23, traceId=tr-0a7b3c
- Analytics API logs: Query served from cache for range 2026-03-10T23:00:00Z-2026-03-11T02:00:00Z, cache_key=hm:brightai:acct-881:20260310-3h
- Sentry events: console.heatmap.refresh.timeout (5 events between 2026-03-09T23:12Z and 2026-03-10T00:03Z)

Attachments:
- Screenshot: img-heatmap-2026-03-09-18-22.png

Notes: Customer mentions they recently switched the account timezone during business hours which appears correlated with when the issue started.

investigation_notes: Checked frontend telemetry: heatmap widget schedules an interval job with an ID stored on widget state. When timezone metadata is updated via account settings broadcast, widget rehydrates state and old interval id is lost without clearing, causing setInterval to stop firing.

Analytics pipeline returns cached responses for identical UTC window queries. When client-side bucket boundaries shift (e.g., account timezone change), the client does not recompute query windows and keeps using a cached UTC window key leading to stale results until a full page reload regenerates cache key.

Hypothesis 1: Frontend bug in widget lifecycle causing refresh timers to be dropped on timezone metadata mutation.
Hypothesis 2: Client query key generation uses UTC start/end times before applying timezone offsets; caching layer uses that key causing stale cache hits when timezone changes.

Queried metrics-store: cache hit rate for heatmap queries rose from 12% to 86% for acct-881 after timezone change window. Suggests stale cache usage.
Related logs: analytics-cache: hit key hm:brightai:acct-881:20260310-3h at 2026-03-10T23:05Z repeated every 30s without underlying query execution.
Reproduced locally: change account timezone from UTC to America/Los_Angeles while dashboard is open -> refresh interval stops after ~10 minutes and cached window keys continue to be used.
resolution:
Workaround provided: asked customer to reload dashboard after changing account timezone and to temporarily set auto-refresh to 60s. Engineering changes: merged frontend patch to stop mutating timezone object and to reliably clear and re-register refresh timers when widget settings change (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5821). Backend cache key generation has been updated to include explicit timezone offset in the cache key for time-windowed queries (internal PR INT-4121).

Deployment notes:
- Frontend patch rolled to staging 2026-03-12 14:30 and to prod canary 2026-03-13 02:00.
- Cache-key change deployed to analytics pipeline canary 2026-03-13 04:00.

Follow-ups:
- INT-4121: Add integration test coverage for widget setting mutations and refresh scheduling.
- Add observability alert to detect rapid loss of scheduled refresh jobs for dashboard widgets.
- Postmortem due 2026-03-20 to capture customer impact and harden migration path for timezone/account metadata changes.
public_response_snippet: Hi BrightAI team — we identified a frontend lifecycle bug that caused the heatmap widget to stop auto-refreshing after an account timezone change and a caching mismatch that returned older UTC-windowed data. We've deployed a fix to prod and a backend cache key change to ensure timezone-aware queries. A full postmortem will be shared. If you still see issues, please let us know and include dashboard id db-78a1.
